newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE - World market for September 10 - Robusta futures in London reversed to end firmer across-the-board, dragged higher by a hefty spot premium and industry bargain hunting. At the close the September contract was up $17 at $1,608 while November added $6 to close at $1,552.

Traders said the spot premium had widened because it seemed the long-holder in September wanted to take delivery of the coffee. However, with the open interest on September at 2,401 lots and the uncovered said to be at some 2,200 lots, a squeeze is unlikely, trader said. It was added that if the premium moves much higher, it will attract more coffee.

In New York arabica futures ended near unchanged after a last-minute round of speculative selling erased the bulk of the day's gains. December finished at 121.85 cents/lb, down 65 points while December added 10 points to close at 111.30 cents/lb. The back months closed 50 points lower to 50 points higher.

Reports that Colombian trucker protests are increasing and that leftist guerrilla activity is picking up aided sentiment as this is causing transport delays. However, many traders remain bearish and believe that December will test the $1.00 barrier.

RAZIL - According to the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (FEBEC), Brazil shipped 1.541 million 60-kg bags of coffee in August 1996, which compares to 1.120 million bags exported the previous month and 739,059 bags shipped in June. Of the August total, 1.369 million bags were arabica coffee, while shipments of robusta coffee reached 171,625 bags. The volume shipped in August is in line with expectations and should not have any impact of the market.

Under the ACPC retention scheme, Brazil can ship an average of 1.5 million bags per month up to the end of this year, given that it has an export allowance of 9 million bags in the first six months of this coffee year. Brazilian sources made clear that the country would not ship more than this amount but would aim to sell much less.
According to the Brazilian Soluble Coffee Association (ABICS) soluble coffee exports in August 1996 reached 230,793 bags, giving a total of 1.54 million bags since the beginning of the year.

FINLAND - Finland imported 78,308 bags of coffee in March 1996, 22 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 201,100 bags, 3.5 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 44 per cent to 758,500 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1996 were Guatemala (21,900 vs 27,800 bags), Brazil (36,900 vs 42,900 bags) and Colombia (65,500 vs 46,300 bags).

The country exported 31,400 bags of coffee in January/March 1996, 32 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply to 96,800 bags from 217,500 bags the previous year.
TANZANIA - Tanzania exported 934,800 bags of coffee in July/June 1995/96 which compares to 611,900 bags the previous year.
Major export markets in July/June 1995/96 were Germany (333,600 vs 180,300 bags), the Netherlands (109,300 vs 50,700 bags) and Japan (188,700 vs 192,600 bags).
